---
title: Projects, Namespaces, and Quotas
---

Our container platform uses resource quotas on *Projects* and *Namespaces*. A quota is a limitation on how many resources a user or group of users can utilize. Kubernetes uses two kinds of resource quotas: *requests* and *limits*. See [Kubernetes documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/) for more information about this concept. Currently applied quotas are on *CPU* and *Memory* resources. These quotas are set on both *Project* and *Namespace*.

The *Personal* Project and default *Namespace* have 20 CPUs *request*, 32 CPUs *limit*, 40GB Memory *requests*, and 64GB Memory *limits*. Other types of quotas are not set. Users can request a new project with significantly larger quotas at [IT Service desk](mailto:k8s@ics.muni.cz).

## Namespaces

Without requesting an explicit project, users are given a *Personal* project with the limits mentioned above. Together with the *Personal* project, a default *Namespace* is created. Both the *Personal* project and the default *Namespace* have the mentioned quotas. The default *Namespace* is set to the exact same quota as the *Personal* project, which means that **any new** *Namespace* is out of available quotas. It is not possible to extend *Personal* project quotas, so there are two options:

1. Request an explicit project.
2. Decrease quotas for the default *Namespace* and allocate spare resources to a new *Namespace*.

### Changing Namespace Quotas

To change resource quotas for an existing namespace, navigate through `Cluster` (1), `Projects/Namespaces` (2), select the `Namespace` (3) context menu and `Edit Config`.

![quotaedit1](/img/ceritsc/quotaedit1.png)

Then you can change `Resource Quotas` for the *Namespace* as desired and `Save` them.

![quotaedit2](/img/ceritsc/quotaedit2.png)

### Creating New Namespaces

To make things work properly, do not create a *Namespace* using `kubectl`, `helm`, or any other tools. It is possible, but you will not see this *Namespace* in the Rancher UI. Instead, use the Rancher UI to create the *Namespace*. Most tools like `helm` and `kustomize` should deal with already existing *Namespaces* just fine.

1. In a project where you want to create a new namespace, lower the namespace resource quotas of some of the existing namespaces to create space for the new namespace. Perform this according to the previous section.

2. Create a new namespace in the project via the UI button and set some resource quotas.

![create-ns](/img/ceritsc/create-ns.png)

3. Create the following role binding in the new namespace. New namespaces are forbidden from performing any action, so to ensure you can deploy objects, this role binding is necessary. You can create a role binding via the UI or using kubectl.

YAML rolebinding:
```yaml title="rolebinding.yaml"
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: [new_namespace_name]-sa-rb
  namespace: [new_namespace_name]
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: grant-namespace-permissions
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: default
  namespace: [new_namespace_name]
```

Kubectl: Change `[new_namespace_name]` for the actual name of your new namespace, save it as e.g. `rolebinding.yaml`, and deploy via `kubectl create -f rolebinding.yaml`

UI: Navigate according to the image and import the same YAML as above, changing `[new_namespace_name]` for the actual name of your new namespace.

![rolebinding](/img/ceritsc/rolebinding.png)

## Resource Limits

If a running container exceeds its limits, the result depends on the resource type. If the resource is CPU, the container continues to run but the CPU is limited, i.e., it runs slower. If the resource is Memory or ephemeral-storage, the container is *evicted*. It can be restarted in the case of a *Deployment*, but the resource is not extended automatically, so eviction is likely to happen again.

## Consequences

* Every Pod, Job, Deployment, and any other kind that runs a container needs the *resources* attribute to be set; otherwise, deployment is rejected with an error similar to:

```bash
Pods "master-685f855ff-gg9sr" is forbidden: failed quota: default-w2qv7: must specify limits.cpu,limits.memory,requests.cpu,requests.memory:Deployment does not have minimum availability.
```

However, this should not happen for users because we set default container resources to 1 CPU and 512MB Memory for both *requests* and *limits*. This default is applied only in cases where users have not specified resources.

* Quotas cannot be overbooked, so the sum of quotas for all namespaces within a *Project* must not be larger than the *Project* quota. As we set the initial *namespace* quota to be equal to the *Project*, there is no room for additional namespaces. Users can create additional namespaces, but they need to decrease quotas on the initial *namespace* first or request an extension of *Project* quotas.

* If users deploy more containers than the quota allows, *Pods* are rejected immediately, while *Jobs* and other types of deployments are pending until there are free resources within the quota.

* Setting quotas on GPU resources is currently not possible.
